purpose: Incremental native PDF suffixes, immutable-prefix Blob reuse, cancellable output, and bypassing unchanged UI page assembly. Full helper removal is deferred at the user request.

findings.workload: Standalone benchmark exports change only the document title while preserving existing page structure, annotations and form values; the offline PWA and synthetic tests separately exercise edited fields and nested replies.
findings.interpretation: Standalone and repeated saves are faster. The two engineering documents have lower standalone peak PSS, but merged full rewrites are 16-32 percent slower and whole-processing peak PSS is 5-8 percent higher than the previous PDFium revision. This is not a universal I/O or memory improvement.

fixtures.description: Raspberry Pi Beginners Guide fifth edition, 288 pages
User-supplied 43-page A0 drawing from previous audit; private fixture not redistributed

method.uiRequestParity: All saves pass the complete page structure and syncFormFields=true, as the UI does. Saved cover previews are tested separately and physical file-write time is excluded.
method.memory: Chromium process PSS/RSS/SwapPSS sampled every 50 ms. Baseline includes original and donor bytes. Retained snapshots follow GC. WASM capacity is not live allocation.
method.execution: Fresh browser per fixture/variant/round; rotated order; no concurrent builds, other tests or validators launched by this task during timing. Host counters retained.

validation.checks: All page counts, dimensions, rotations, annotation subtype counts, reply parents/states/flags, popup ownership, link targets/URIs, form values and edited title. Independent pdf-lib structure checks and Poppler text/1200px raster samples.

cancellationDuringBuild.note: Additional correctness run with concurrent builds; latency is not comparable with idle diagnostics.

checks.application: 809/809 in 100 files at cf6b29b; after the unchanged-assembly follow-up, all 202 PDF tests in 24 files passed again; 25 focused export/reply tests passed after the cache policy change.
checks.sdk: 61/61 in 8 files, including multi-chunk delta cancellation, redaction rollback, xref streams/tables, repaired/nonzero-generation/encrypted fallback and repeated reopened revisions.

limitations: Export time measures generating the full output Blob. The native writer generates a suffix, but filesystem saving still writes the complete Blob; in-place filesystem append is not implemented.

Incremental output retains prior form values, annotations and metadata in its original prefix. Full rewrite is available with incremental:false and is forced for page structure changes, flattening, encryption/unsafe xrefs and native text redaction.

One original Blob is cached per live input byte array to speed repeated saves. This retains original-byte storage until its weak key can be collected or a full rewrite evicts it; browser Blob storage is outside the WASM working buffer.
Cancellation is cooperative: the caller rejects promptly but graph preparation or a single large native object can delay worker readiness. No hard 8 ms bound is claimed.
Only three real documents on Chromium/Linux ARM64 with software rendering; no universal PDF, GPU, Windows or Tauri runtime performance claim.
Visual validation samples pages rather than rasterizing every page. Synthetic tests cover editable forms, encryption, redaction and nested annotations absent from parts of the real corpus.
The offline PWA run retains the previously observed revoked Blob image request failure; there were no page exceptions or visible broken images.
pdf-lib authoring helpers remain for the next round; pdfjs-dist remains a development validation/comparison dependency with no runtime source imports.
